later_comparison.finding: Al-Alusi preserves Ata's Abu Lahab attribution while identifying al-As ibn Wa'il as the majority view.

english_fidelity.finding: English preserves Ata, Abu Lahab, the son's death, and Muhammad has been cut off (i.e., from progeny) tonight. The parenthetical gloss separates cut off from tonight; the prior literal phrase search missed it.
english_fidelity.policy: Preserve this narrative alignment while retaining absent chain and unresolved direct Ibn Abi Hatim edition.

explicit_absences: No chain accompanies the Ata attribution in the checked Ibn Kathir excerpt.
No direct Ibn Abi Hatim edition, page, report number, or chain was located in the bounded public search.
Al-Suyuti's attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim is an index-level trace, not a direct-source verification.
The later al-Alusi comparison is not treated as an independent early witness.
The Ata/Abu Lahab alternative remains separate from 108-I10-R02 Ibn Abbas/Abu Jahl and from the al-As ibn Wa'il majority view.
No authentication ruling, new proposition, or database publication is authorized.

superseded_fidelity.finding: The live English entry preserves Ata, Abu Lahab, and the death of the Messenger's son, but the bounded check does not find the explicit statement that Muhammad was cut off that night.
superseded_fidelity.policy: Record bounded English coverage without inferring omitted attribution, actor, or occasion wording.
